title: Bluetooth Key Finders as Gifts: Which Tracker Fits Which Phone, and What They Can't Find
subtitle: A plain-English guide to Apple AirTag and Tile Mate: how they work, what they cost, and the limits worth knowing before you wrap one.
excerpt: Small Bluetooth trackers can help find lost keys, wallets and remotes. The right one depends mostly on whether the person uses an iPhone or an Android phone.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Most of us know the routine. You are ready to leave, and the car keys are not on the hook. Ten minutes later they turn up in yesterday's coat pocket, and by then you are running late and a little rattled.

A Bluetooth item finder is a small tag that attaches to keys or other everyday items, such as a bag. When something goes missing, your phone can make the tag ring if you are close enough. It can be a practical gift for someone who often hunts for keys, as long as the limits below are clear.

Bluetooth is a short-range wireless link, the same kind that connects wireless headphones to a phone. The tracker works with your phone through a free app. When you are nearby, you use the app to make the tag play a sound so you can follow it to the sofa cushions.

These are Bluetooth finders, not GPS (the satellite system a car navigator uses). They work only when your phone, or another device in the maker's network, is close enough to the tag. If nothing in the network comes near it, the tag cannot be found.

Range is shorter than the box suggests. In its review of the 2024 Tile Mate, Tom's Guide noted a listed range of 350 feet but measured about 60 feet. The Tile Mate sold on the Home Depot page below is the older 2020 model, and we could not verify its range, so treat the 2024 figures as a guide only. Plan on finding things within a room or two, not across a parking lot.

The single biggest choice is the phone. Apple's AirTag works only with iPhone (and Apple Watch, through the Find My app). Tile works with both iPhone and Android phones. Before buying, quietly find out which phone the person carries.

items: Phone match: AirTag is for iPhone owners; Tile works on iPhone and Android.

Fees: Apple's AirTag page lists no subscription. Tile's basic app is free. Its optional Premium plan adds extras such as separation alerts, which are meant to warn you when you leave something behind. Tom's Guide listed Premium at $30 a year in May 2025 and said alerts can arrive late. We could not verify Tile's own current pricing, so check current price.

Battery: Tom's Guide says the 2024 Tile Mate has a sealed battery that lasts about three years, so you replace the whole tag rather than recharge it. We could not verify the battery life of the 2020 model sold at Home Depot.

Newer iPhone features: AirTag's Precision Finding, which helps guide you to the tag, works only with certain newer iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple's page lists iPhone Air or iPhone 15 or later (not iPhone 16e or 17e) and Apple Watch Series 9 or later or Ultra 2 or later. Someone with an older iPhone may not get it.
Buttons and grip: these tags are small. If fingers are stiff, check how easy the button is to press and how the tag attaches to a key ring.
Loudness: Apple says the newest AirTag has its loudest speaker yet. If hearing is a concern, an audiologist is the right person to ask.
Returns: Home Depot lists a 90-day in-store return window for the Tile Mate. Keep receipts with gifts.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well

Setup is the part a grown child or grandchild can help with over the holidays. Open the app (Find My for AirTag, the free Tile app for Tile) and follow the maker's setup instructions, since the steps can differ by model and phone. Give each tag a clear name, such as "House keys" or "Blue wallet," so there is no guessing later.

Then practice once together. Hide the keys, open the app and ring them. It is far easier to learn when nothing is actually lost. Tile also works the other way: Tom's Guide says you double-press the tag's button to ring your phone, and the Home Depot page says it can find your phone even on silent.

Any tracker can be misused to follow a person. Android phones now warn people when an unknown Bluetooth tracker is traveling with them, and Apple has similar protections for AirTags. These alerts are not foolproof: a third-party tool has been reported that can permanently disable an AirTag's alert sound. If a warning ever appears on your phone, take it seriously and check your bag, coat and car. If you feel unsafe, call your local police, and in an emergency, call 911.

An item finder is for keys and wallets, not for people. It is not a medical alert and cannot call for help after a fall. If you need that kind of safety, ask your doctor and look at a monitored medical alert device. In an emergency, call 911.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: "Unlike the Tile Pro and its replaceable battery, the Tile Mate is completely sealed up." (Philip Michaels, Tom's Guide, reviewing the 2024 Tile Mate)

A tracker will not stop keys from wandering off, but it can turn a frantic search into a quick tap and a beep. Match it to the right phone, set it up together, and it can make a thoughtful gift for busy mornings.

products.name: Apple AirTag, 4-pack
products.blurb: Suits iPhone owners, using the Find My app on iPhone or Apple Watch, with no subscription listed. Apple says it has its loudest speaker yet, and free engraving is offered only at Apple, with free shipping at apple.com.

products.name: Tile Mate (2020), 1 Pack, RE-19001
products.blurb: Suits Android users or mixed-phone households, since Tile works with both iPhone and Android. It uses the free Tile app and can find your phone even on silent. This is the 2020 model; the range and battery figures in this article come from a review of the 2024 model and may differ.
